Risotto is a classic Italian rice dish where short-grain rice is cooked slowly with broth until it achieves a characteristically creamy texture, often flavored with onion, wine, butter, and Parmesan cheese. It is believed to have originated in Lombardy, with the first identifiable recipe dating from 1809. The dish relies on specific high-starch rice varieties like Arborio, Carnaroli, and Vialone Nano, which release starch during cooking. The standard preparation involves first toasting the rice in fat (tostatura), then gradually adding hot broth while stirring constantly, and finishing by beating in cold butter and cheese (mantecatura). Properly cooked risotto is served all'onda (wavy) and is traditionally a primo, though some variations like risotto alla milanese can be a one-course meal.
